title: Trigonometry: Problems in Two and Three Dimensions
summary: Solve problems in two and three dimensions by combining right-angled trigonometry with the sine, cosine and area rules, including heights, distances and angles in space.

items: Identify the triangles in the diagram: usually one **vertical** triangle (with the height) and one **horizontal** triangle (on the ground).
Mark right angles: a vertical tower is perpendicular to every line on the ground through its foot.
Find a common side shared by the two triangles.
Use right-angled trigonometry in the right-angled triangle and the sine or cosine rule in the other.
Keep answers in terms of the given variables if asked to 'show that' or 'prove'.

notes.caption: A vertical tower TF with its foot F on horizontal ground; A and B are points on the ground

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A and B are two points on level ground, 80 m apart. TF is a vertical tower with foot F. $\hat{FAB} = 40^\circ$, $\hat{ABF} = 65^\circ$, and the angle of elevation of T from A is $25^\circ$. Find the height of the tower.

notes.title: Worked example 2: in terms of variables
notes.problem: In △ABC on horizontal ground, $AB = x$, $\hat{A} = \alpha$ and $\hat{ACB} = \beta$. CD is a vertical pole at C with angle of elevation $\theta$ from B. Show that $CD = \dfrac{x\sin\alpha\tan\theta}{\sin\beta}$.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In 'show that' questions, work only with the letters given. Do not substitute numbers until the question asks you to calculate.

rows: Non-right-angled, two sides and included angle, or three sides

questions.prompt: A vertical pole is perpendicular to every line on horizontal ground that passes through its foot.
In a horizontal triangle you know two angles and one side. Which rule finds another side?
From a point 60 m from the foot of a vertical tower the angle of elevation is $32^\circ$. Find the height, correct to two decimal places.
Points A and B on the ground are 50 m and 70 m from point C, and $\hat{ACB} = 60^\circ$. Find AB, correct to two decimal places.
In △ABF on level ground, $AB = 100$ m, $\hat{A} = 50^\circ$ and $\hat{B} = 70^\circ$. Find BF (opposite $\hat{A}$), correct to two decimal places.

P and Q are 120 m apart on level ground. R is the foot of a vertical tower RT. $\hat{RPQ} = 52^\circ$ and $\hat{PQR} = 68^\circ$. The angle of elevation of T from Q is $20^\circ$. Calculate the height of the tower.

In △ABC (horizontal), $BC = d$, $\hat{B} = x$ and $\hat{C} = y$. AD is a vertical pole at A, and the angle of elevation of D from B is $\theta$. Show that $AD = \dfrac{d\sin y\tan\theta}{\sin(x + y)}$.
questions.memo:
✓ $\hat{A} = 180^\circ - (x + y)$, so $\sin A = \sin(x + y)$ (1)
✓ $\frac{AB}{\sin y} = \frac{d}{\sin(x + y)}$ (1)
✓ $AB = \frac{d\sin y}{\sin(x + y)}$ (1)
✓ $AD = AB\tan\theta$ (1)

questions.prompt: A triangular piece of land has sides 45 m and 60 m with included angle $110^\circ$. Find its area, correct to two decimal places.
A 25 m vertical mast stands at C. B is 40 m from C on level ground. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the mast from B.
Why is it important to identify a side common to two triangles in a 3D problem?
questions.memo:
✓ The common side links the two triangles (1)
✓ It is found in one triangle and then used to solve the other (1)
